subject: Hosted API commit tier reshuffle + burst-to-commit conversion
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@fluxretail.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API commit tier reshuffle + burst-to-commit conversion

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time to walk through Flux Retail's usage patterns last week. Based on the recent telemetry and your Q2 product roadmap, I sketched a pragmatic renewal approach that: (1) converts a portion of your current burst credits into a predictable monthly commit, and (2) introduces a two‑tier rate ladder with a higher committed rate and a lower overage rate for seasonal spikes.

Key proposal (high level):
- Monthly committed tokens: 1.5B tokens/month (migrated from 800M burst + 700M new commit)
- Billing bands: committed vs. overage (committed priced at $2.75 / 1K tokens-equivalent; overage capped at $3.40 / 1K within 25% of monthly committed)
- Soft throttle and burst buffer: 10% temporary burst cushion before fallback to overage pricing
- Proration: May will be pro‑rated for the conversion window (we'll credit unused burst at current rate against May invoice)
- Operational SLAs: 99.9% uptime for committed lanes; canary fallback to a lower-cost model if regional capacity is constrained

Action items I need from you to finalize the SOW:
1) Confirmation that the 1.5B/month committed baseline fits your forecast for Q3–Q4 (we can stage to 1.0B then step to 1.5B if preferred)
2) Preferred invoice cadence (monthly vs. quarterly advance)
3) PO guidelines or procurement contacts for final signatures

I've attached a draft renewal (Flux_Renewal_Draft_2025.pdf) and an SOW excel that maps expected monthly ramps by product team. If the high level looks good, I'll route the legal-friendly amendment for your procurement team and include a short appendix describing the burst-to-commit conversion mechanics.

Quick note on routing: Kimberly is looped in to confirm banked-burst accounting and billing proration; Vivek can confirm the latency SLAs and any region-specific routing constraints.

Thanks — talk soon.

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0183

Attachments: Flux_Renewal_Draft_2025.pdf (Renewal draft), SOW-hosted-uplift.xlsx (token ramp breakdown)
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@fluxretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Flux Retail Procurement <procurement@fluxretail.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit tier reshuffle + burst-to-commit conversion

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear write-up. The approach makes sense; two quick clarifications from our side before we loop procurement formally: 

1) The committed baseline: can you provide a 3‑month staging option (1.0B -> 1.25B -> 1.5B) with proration at each step? Several product features ramp in July and we'd prefer not to overcommit immediately.
2) Overage pricing: is the $3.40 /1K a hard cap for the season, or does it float if we exceed 125% of committed in a month? We need a predictable top-line to model costs into the merchant pricing.
3) Invoice cadence: procurement prefers quarterly advance for vendors with annual commitments — can you model the numbers for quarterly billing and include payment terms (net 30 standard, but curious about a 45-day option)

Procurement (cc'd) — Elena and I would prefer a single amendment that describes the burst conversion and the staged commit ladder; once procurement confirms PO formatting, we'll send a redline request.

Also, Vivek — any concerns about latency if we stage up quickly in US-West? We rely on sub-100ms median tail for checkout flows.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Product Ops | Flux Retail
elena.ruiz@fluxretail.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@fluxretail.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Flux Retail Procurement <procurement@fluxretail.com>
Date: Fri, 16 May 2025 14:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit tier reshuffle + burst-to-commit conversion

Elena / team —

Thanks — all good questions. Short answers below and I'll attach an updated SOW with the 3‑month staging and the two billing cadence views (monthly vs quarterly advance).

1) Staged commit ramp: yes — we'll include a staged option: May‑July proration at 1.0B / 1.25B / 1.5B. We'll compute credits for any unused burst pro‑rata and apply to the first quarterly invoice.

2) Overage cap: the $3.40 /1K is a contracted cap for overage usage up to 125% of committed. Above 125% we'll move to an escalated overage band ($4.25 /1K) to protect capacity fairness — we'll make that explicit in section 4.3 of the amendment. If you expect sustained >125% usage, let's discuss increasing the committed baseline instead.

3) Invoice cadence: quarterly advance is fine. We can offer Net 45 for the first year of the renewal for established customers; otherwise standard Net 30 applies. I'll include both pricing tables in the SOW for procurement to pick.

Vivek — can you confirm no additional routing configuration required for US-West beyond the capacity staging? If we need a dedicated pool for Flux's committed lane, call it out and we'll price a small uplift.

Next steps: I will (A) upload the updated SOW and staged ramp pricing to the Drive link and (B) route an amendment for legal's quick review by EOD Monday. If procurement is ready, send the preferred PO template and we'll attach to the redline.

Jordan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
